title: Smoothed retroactive quota attribution for late streaming events
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: We continue to see sharp, short-duration spikes in per-model daily token charts after edge proxies backfill delayed streaming events. These spikes are not actual immediate customer consumption but retrospective attributions applied to historical time windows. The Console charts currently place backfilled tokens at the ingest timestamp (now), which inflates the current day and under-represents the original windows. This confuses customers and triggers false billing alerts and quota breaches for rolling windows.

Scope: Fix the presentation and accounting for late/retroactive streaming token events across the Console and per-model breakdowns without changing the canonical per-customer billing numbers until finance signs off on retroactive adjustments. The ticket covers: (1) algorithm to apportion late events into historical buckets (when event contained original_request_time), (2) UI markers for backfill-adjusted points in Console charts, (3) a backfill job that re-assigns ingestion to original windows for analytics only, (4) safe roll-forward strategy that avoids double-counting with existing backfill pipeline.

Goals:
- Make Console charts reflect token consumption in the appropriate historical buckets when original timestamps are available.
- Smooth visualization so short bursts from large backfills don't create multi-day customer-facing anomalies.
- Provide explicit provenance (badge/tooltip) for any chart bars/points that were adjusted due to backfill.
- Keep canonical billing ledger unchanged until finance-approved migration; provide diff reports.

Constraints and considerations:
- Some incoming events lack original_request_time; these must continue to be attributed at ingestion time but flagged.
- Must work with streaming prefix tokens where KV cache attribution is non-trivial.
- Avoid large, immediate writes to timeseries store that could overwhelm the aggregation job.
- Rollback must be possible in case of mis-attribution.

Non-goals: Do not perform any automatic customer invoice changes in this ticket. Do not alter quota enforcement behavior for live requests; this is an analytics and console correction first.
acceptance_criteria: Console per-model daily and hourly charts show tokens attributed to original request windows when original_request_time is present
A legend/badge appears on charts for any points that were modified by retroactive attribution explaining the backfill reason
Backfill re-assignment job produces a reconciliation report (counts by model and day) and a safe-preview diff before applying to production charts
No customer-facing quota enforcement behavior changes as a result of the analytics backfill; live quota checks continue to use ingestion-time tallies
Automated tests cover: events with and without original_request_time, streaming prefix token attribution, and idempotency of repeated backfills
Runbook and rollback steps documented and validated in staging with a representative backfill dataset
plan_steps: Investigate event payloads to enumerate timestamp fields (ingest_time, original_request_time, forwarded_time) and failure modes

Design attribution algorithm: prefer original_request_time, fall back to ingest_time, clamp attribution to model-enabled windows, and distribute large batched events across nearest historical minute boundaries to avoid 1-2s spikes
Prototype data transformation script (Spark) that converts raw events -> adjusted timeseries and produces reconciliation diffs
Add provenance metadata tags to timeseries store for adjusted points (chart_only=true, backfill_job_id/<id>, original_ts)
Frontend: add visual markers and tooltip text; ensure legend copy remains concise and links to help center article
Create staging backfill run and validate charts against ground-truth samples; iterate on smoothing parameters
Schedule controlled production backfill with throttling and monitoring; publish reconciliation report to finance and account teams
Post-run: validate console charts, run alert suppression for known adjustment windows, and update runbook
monitoring_playbook: Monitor reconciliation runner metrics: processed_events_per_minute, adjusted_points_per_minute, reassign_errors
Dashboards: reconciliation-preview (expected vs adjusted tokens), per-model delta heatmap, and ingestion-to-original-timespan distribution
Alerts: >5% of model-day tokens changed for customer with >$10k/month spend -> page on-call; reconciliation_job_failures -> SLO-based page
Soft-alert suppression: suppress quota-alerts for customers with an open backfill_preview until migration is approved
